pages.text: Graphite electrodes have a much higher resistance than copper or zinc ones: $(item)300 ohm$() each, against 10.
Each holder still needs at least $(item)5 A$() (the server setting electrolysisMinimumCurrent), and current is voltage divided by resistance:
$(li)5 A x 300 ohm = $(item)1500 V$() at the very least on every holder,$(li)the holder breaks above $(item)20000 V$(), so stay between the two.
At 1500 V each holder draws about 7.5 kW, so three of them need a serious power plant. Plan your generators and transformers before building the furnace.

Power goes in through the $(item)top face$() of each holder, like for electrolysis. If one holder is under 5 A, it counts as a broken machine and the whole furnace stops: check each holder with a multimeter, it says when the current is too low.
A low voltage is the most common reason an arc furnace does nothing, well before the ingredients.
